tasks.entryDescription: Nested closed balls with radii→0; complete metric space plus Cauchy construction; locally compact Hausdorff/open-set formulation.
tasks.currentSketch: Assume a complete metric space M is the union of closed sets C_n, each with empty interior. Starting with a point in C₁, choose a point outside C₁ and a small closed ball around it disjoint from C₁. Inductively choose nested centers and radii shrinking by a fixed factor, with the kth ball disjoint from C_k. The centers are Cauchy; completeness gives a limit lying in every nested ball, hence outside every C_k, contradicting the assumed cover.

tasks.entryDescription: Nested closed balls with radii→0; complete metric space plus Cauchy construction; locally compact Hausdorff/open-set formulation.
tasks.currentSketch: In a locally compact Hausdorff space, suppose a nonempty open set is covered by countably many closed sets with empty interior. Choose a nonempty relatively compact open subset avoiding the first closed set; within it choose one avoiding the second, and so on, with nested compact closures. Compactness gives a point in all closures, contradicting the cover.

tasks.currentSketch: Choose a countable dense set {x_j} in compact metric K. Boundedness lets diagonal extraction make f_n(x_j) converge for every j. Equicontinuity and finite ε-nets upgrade pointwise convergence on the dense set to uniform Cauchy convergence, hence a uniformly convergent subsequence.

tasks.currentSketch: Uniform boundedness plus equicontinuity implies a finite ε-net of functions in C(K): cover K by finitely many small balls and quantize the bounded values at their centers. Thus the family is totally bounded; completeness of C(K) gives sequential compactness.

tasks.entryDescription: Diagonal subsequence on a dense countable set plus equicontinuity; finite ε-net/total boundedness; compactness in C(K).
tasks.currentSketch: In C(K), Arzelà–Ascoli says relative compactness is equivalent to pointwise relative compactness plus equicontinuity (for compact K). The compactness statement itself is an application/consequence, so it is not a separate proof unless a compactness criterion is independently established.

tasks.entryDescription: Ultrafilter convergence; Alexander subbase theorem; choice/finite intersection property.
tasks.currentSketch: An ultrafilter on ∏X_i projects to an ultrafilter on each compact X_i, which converges to x_i. Every basic product neighborhood constrains finitely many coordinates, so belongs to the original ultrafilter; thus it converges to (x_i), proving product compactness.

tasks.entryDescription: Ultrafilter convergence; Alexander subbase theorem; choice/finite intersection property.
tasks.currentSketch: Alexander subbase theorem: if every cover by subbasic open sets has a finite subcover, the space is compact. For a product, a cover by subbasic cylinders with no finite subcover would induce coordinate closed sets with the finite intersection property, contradicting compactness of a factor; equivalently use the standard subbase proof.

tasks.entryDescription: Ultrafilter convergence; Alexander subbase theorem; choice/finite intersection property.
tasks.currentSketch: A family of closed subsets of the product with the finite intersection property is extended to an ultrafilter by choice. Its coordinate projections converge by compactness of each factor; the coordinate limit point belongs to every closed set in the family. This is the closed-set/choice formulation of the ultrafilter proof.
